recipes.name: Quinoa and Black Bean Chili
ingredients_raw: 2 (19 ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained
1 tablespoon minced chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring water and quinoa to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until quinoa is tender and water has been absorbed, about 15 to 20 minutes. Set aside.

Meanwhile, heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion; cook and stir until onion softens and turns translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic, chili powder, and cumin; cook and stir for 1 minute to release the flavors. Stir in black beans, tomatoes, bell peppers, zucchini, jalapeño pepper, chipotle pepper, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in quinoa and corn. Cook until corn is heated through, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in cilantro, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Quinoa and Black Bean Chili
raw_recipe.description: This tasty vegetarian quinoa and black bean chili is loaded with vegetables and spices, with jalapeño and chipotle peppers to add a little smoky heat.

review.reviewBody: Wow, why has no one tried and rated this recipe yet? Yay! I am first! :D This is an absolute EXCELLENT Vegetarian Chili option! with the inclusion of the quinoa, you do not miss the meat and it is SO healthy for you. I made a couple changes, I used vegetable broth to cook my quinoa in as opposed to water (I always do and it lends a nice flavour to the quinoa), and used red quinoa as I prefer that over the plain. I also used Ground Chipotle Chili Powder instead of regular chili powder as I love the smoky flavour it brings to the dish. To make this even more healthy and to cut out as much sodium as possible, I used dried beans (re-hydrated) and instead of the canned/crushed tomatoes, I chopped up 4 large roma tomatoes, oops, one more, I left out the zucchini as I am not a fan of that vegetable. Otherwise, followed the recipe exactly with all the other ingredients and it is spicy with the inclusion of the jalapeno and the chipotle, so adjust to your liking if you are not a fan of too much heat. This does make a large pot worth, so I just divided it up into 2 cup portions and froze them, these will make great meals on the fly, just serve with some cornbread or a salad! Thanks Shauna for the great recipe! a clear winner here! :D

I have made this many times, just getting around to writing a review. (Making a batch for the superbowl!) I make this almost as written, with a couple of slight changes. I don't like green pepper, so I use a red and a yellow, which enhances the color of the dish. I roast the jalapeño in my toaster oven before adding it to the chili to give it a smoky taste and mellow it out. When I make ahead, I freeze the cooked veg mix and the quinoa separately, so it doesn't get even thicker. Then I add the corn at the end, as written. My big tip is to use the jarred Frontera Chipotle Pepper Adobo sauce. I keep a jar in the fridge and use it in any recipe that calls for adobo.

I made this and shared some with a friend who immediately asked me for the recipe. I went totally lazy with it and made it in the slow cooker. I did not precook any of the veg or quinoa, and cooked on high for five hours, it was great! I just added the quinoa in dry and added in the veg broth I'd have used to cook the quinoa in with everything else. I used a can of Rotel rather than messing with the raw jalapeño, and that worked out great, too. It didn't look terribly promising when I put it together, but by dinner time, it was super yummy, and kind of a lighter version of chili, good for a warmer day. It's going in the "keeper" file. Thanks for sharing!

I added 1LB minced beef as Hubby is a meat lover, of course browned it first and excess the fat as much as possible. Sautéed one small chili, onion&garlic and spice, put them and set-aside beef together in slow cooker, along with other ingredients except quinoa, cilantro, peppers as peppers would get bitter if cooked too long. Cooked on low for 4 hrs when I was at gym, added the rest, cooked on high for 1/2hr. Served with sour cream and corn dog casserole also from this site. Hubby really likes it, however I found it was a bit bland for me so I added some chipotle Tabasco on my own plate.(Probably bcoz I didn’t add jalapeño as I didn’t hv any on hand) Anyway it was tasty and healthy, would be in my weekly rotation!

I made this for the first time with the intention to make something healthy AND that my boyfriend would like and this was a hit. I read a lot of the reviews and this is what I ended up doing: 1. Clean quinoa thoroughly, draining it till water ran clear, which took a few minutes. 2. Soaked it while cutting veggies 3. Cut whole onion, a bunch of cilantro (more than a cup cus we love the stuff), cut two whole tomatoes and seasoned two can of black beans with a little adobo - All while sautéing the onions till they got brown. 4. Added garlic after onions were brown for a few mins then added the quinoa and seasoned. 5. Added chicken broth and simmered. 6. Added a little more cilantro and cayenne pepper then added frozen sweet corn (which was thawing while I was cutting veggies) after 18 mins of quinoa cooking for five more mins7. Added two cups of beans (which I really liked and it was a great balance - I read a lot of people used only one can) 8. Simmer for five more mins and served it with Korean flavored BBQ chicken on top of tortilla with kale and American cheese (sort of like a burrito). Yummmeeeee. We have leftovers for days but I'm looking forward To it.

Excellent hearty, healthy, gluten-free vegetarian dish. Perfect for the winter and very tasty - makes 6-8 servings. Generally followed the recipe but like others, I cooked my quinoa in vegetable stock and also needed at least 2 cups more stock when I added the crushed tomatoes. After adding the quinoa, I could definitely have used even more stock if I had it. I did not add the jalapeno and found there was enough heat for us with the 1 Tbs of chipotle in adobo (I freeze the can in tablespoon dollops in a zip lock so always handy). Served with grated sharp cheddar, Greek yogurt and tortilla chips for dipping. A keeper!

Delicious! I threw everything in a slow cooker (omitting the oil), including uncooked quinoa (make sure to rinse quinoa if not pre-rinsed). I used 2 cups of chicken stock rather than water and canned corn rather than frozen. Cooked on low for at least 5 or 6 hours.

Holey Moley, this was fantastic! I made it per the recipe with only a few exceptions. Like many other reviewers, I cooked my quinoa in vegetable broth to give it more flavor. I added the juice of one lime after all other ingredients were simmering. Then I served it with sliced avocado and it was perfect. Rarely does my husband and 18yo son give me a two thumbs up for a vegan meal, but they did for this meal. I will be returning to this meal over and over again. I only wish I had found this recipe during football season!

First time trying a vegetarian chili. It was really good! We were going to make a big pot for dinner with friends who are vegetarians, but since our plans fell through we added some ground turkey for even more protein (we couldn't really even taste the turkey, so it easily can be left out). We like our chili a little less on the chunky side and more on the soupy side so we added three cans of tomato sauce, and cooked it in the crockpot for a couple of hours. With the added tomato sauce we also upped the chili powder. It came out delicious and there are a ton of leftovers, which we'll freeze for dinners later on. The only thing I'd change is using less onion, which I found to overwhelm some of the bites a little bit, but that's a personal preference.

This is an amazing recipe! I did add my own little touches of course. First I used all organic ingredients. I also omitted the zucchini and the corn. I sautéed the veggies all together instead of separately, added some of the bean liquid and then the spices. Then I added the tomatoe sauce and beans. I also added a little cayenne for some more heat. I used rainbow quinoa and cooked it with some sautéed onions and garlic and used half chicken broth half water for more flavor. I simmered the chili for about 35-40 mins total. The chili was topped with spinach, tomatoes, avocado and some shredded cheddar cheese. Absolutely delicious. My boyfriend and I are newer to quinoa and he was avoiding this dish since it was meatless but when I finally made it he loved it!

This is a favorite in the winter months as an alternative to traditional chili. Has a great smoky flavor. We will occasionally omit the jalapeño and I also cook the quinoa in broth for extra flavor (as other reviewers suggested). I often add garlic base to the recipe as well as we are garlic lovers. We often serve with corn bread, cheese, avocado and cilantro or green onions.
I love the flavors and knowing what a healthy meal this is. It thickened up too much for my taste.
This is a favorite recipe of my son, who is a college student. This chili is flavorful and healthy. Leftovers reheat well. The two of us make three meals out of one batch.
I didn’t have zucchini so I added an additional pepper. So delicious.
I agree with Denise. Kinda bland. Try another chili here. Sweet potato black bean chili. Delicious.

I absolutely love this recipe! It's so flavorful, healthy, has a lot of important fiber, and a good amount of protein. I'm not a vegan or vegetarian, however, I do like to eat a lot of plant based food which focuses on complete protein, and fiber. This a definitely a winner!
Very good. I did leave out the jalapenos and chipotles and added smoked paprika. Is a definite do-again.
I am surprised at all of the positive reviews of this dish. It was very bland and not spicy at all. I had to add hot sauce, cilantro, cheese and sour cream. I won’t make this one a second time.
